entries.title: Ezra 3:2
segments:
Jeshua; he was grandson of Seraiah, who was high-priest at the taking of Jerusalem. 
 
The establishment of the worship and ordinances of God is the surest safeguard against enemies, and the best preparation for all the dispensations of Providence.

entries.title: Ezra 3:3
segments: Fear was upon them; and they put themselves under the special protection of the Almighty by establishing among them his worship.

entries.title: Ezra 3:5
segments: A free-will offering; in addition to what was required in the law.

entries.title: Ezra 3:7
segments:
Joppa; a seaport about forty miles west of Jerusalem. 
 
Money given for the establishment and support of divine worship, instead of being lost, as some think, is most profitably used, and invested where it will yield an abundant reward.

entries.title: Ezra 3:11
segments: Success in all good undertakings comes from the Lord, and the glory should be given to him.  Compare

entries.title: Ezra 3:12
segments:
Wept; at the remembrance of the glory of the former temple, which was now in ruins. 
 
Men are often more affected by what they want, than with what they have; and thus weep and lament, when they ought to rejoice and render praise.
